correctness.rationale: Solving the two-boundary difference equation gives H=p/Σ_i T_i, including the probability p of taking the initial step. For fixed p in (0,1), ε log T_floor(u/ε) converges uniformly on compact u-intervals to F(p,u). Its strictly increasing u-derivative gives the stated sign split. When F(p,t)>0 the final term, even at index floor(t/ε)−1, grows exponentially. When F(p,t)<0, the early terms are uniformly geometrically bounded and converge termwise, and the remaining O(1/ε) terms are exponentially small by uniform negativity away from zero. Thus the positive exceedance limit is 2p−1 below t_c(p) and zero above it. This proves conditional weak convergence at its continuity points for each fixed p and hence joint convergence by integrating bounded test functions; replacing a floor by a ceiling at a fixed positive continuity threshold gives the same limits. Strict decrease of F in p and continuity at p=1 (integrable log singularity at u=0) give the unique increasing inverse p_t. Integration gives p_t(1−p_t), the 3/4 atom, absence of an atom at the upper endpoint, and the marked density by normalization. At the upper edge, on a fixed small u-interval, 1/u−1/(e^u−1) is bounded; the difference between the two corresponding log(1+δ·) integrals is therefore O(δ). The model integral gives δ log(1/δ)+O(δ) uniformly near t_*, and the positive derivative in t at t_* yields the stated edge constant by inversion. Independent numerical integration gives t_*=1.7054281548003088645…; this is corroboration, not proof. The provided checker and recorded output were inspected without running the supplied script.

value.rationale: This extracts an explicit single-excursion scaling law from an exact but ε-dependent hitting formula. The phase boundary separates microscopic from macroscopic excursions conditional on p, and the mixed law predicts both the bias of environments seen in tall excursions and a logarithmically thinned upper edge, which cannot be read from a support bound alone.
